test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 3 hours and 18 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 72 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill three-fourth of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total capacity of the cistern be the LCM of 3, 18, and 72 ⇒ 72 units.

Efficiencies: Tap A = 24, Tap B = 4, Tap C = −1 ⇒ Combined efficiency = 24 + 4 − 1 = 27 units/hour.

Three-fourth capacity of cistern = 72 × (3/4) = 54 units.

Required time = 54 ÷ 27 = 2 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by first tap (A) to fill = 3 hours

Time taken by second tap (B) to fill = 18 hours

Time taken by third tap (C) to empty = 72 hours

 
 

 
 **Tap** 
 **Time (Hours)**

 A (Filling)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B, and C = 24 + 4 − 1 = 27 units/hour

⇒ 3/4th of the total cistern capacity = 72 × (3/4) = 54 units

⇒ Time required to fill 3/4th capacity = 54 ÷ 27 = 2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills a tank and has positive efficiency, while an outlet pipe empties it and has negative efficiency.

Combined Rate Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours, pipe B fills in y hours, and pipe C empties in z hours, the net work done in one hour is (1/x) + (1/y) − (1/z).</p
